text:
Mike T.: Hey folks — running into an onboarding pain with the Go SDK generator sample. When I cancel the context while the generator is streaming, the goroutine often stays alive and CPU creeps up. Repro is tiny: start stream, wait one token, cancel ctx. Expected: generator returns quickly. Observed: hangs until server finishes or timeout.

Mike T.: Repro snippet:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
iter, err := client.Generator(ctx, req)
if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
go func() {
    for {
        tok, err := iter.Next()
        if err != nil { break }
        t.Log(tok.Text)
    }
}()
// cancel immediately
cancel()
// wait and check goroutine count
```

Anya R.: ugh, that is annoying. quick Q: are you using the http transport or gRPC?

Mike T.: http transport in the sample app. I tried with a custom transport that cancels the request, but the SDK seems to reattempt auth and re-open the stream, so cancel doesn't fully stop things.

Kevin L.: Right — we have retry-on-401 logic that triggers token refresh + request retry at the transport layer. For unary calls that's fine, but for streaming it effectively starts a new stream after cancel if the refresh races in.

Nora S.: This is an SDK parity issue we didn't fully spec for Go generators. Node/py have slightly different semantics (they abort on ctx cancel). We need explicit handling: when ctx is Done(), close underlying connection and return a sentinel error (context.Canceled) to the iterator.

Anya R.: Could be two fixes: 1) short-term: change sample-app to call `iter.Close()` / `resp.Body.Close()` on cancel, add `select { case <-ctx.Done(): return }` in the read loop; 2) longer: change transport retry policy to never retry for streaming requests, or make retries opt-in per call.

Mike T.: For the sample update I added a small cancel wrapper that calls `iter.Stop()` (not ideal, it's an ad-hoc method). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/pull/123 (WIP).

Kevin L.: We should avoid ad-hoc Stop. SDK should expose an explicit `Close()` or make the iterator implement `io.Closer` so callers can `defer iter.Close()` and Close will close network stream and drain.

Nora S.: Agree. Proposal:
- API: `type GeneratorIterator interface { Next() (Token, error); Close() error }`
- Transport: when Close or ctx.Done, cancel the http.Request context + suppress auth retry path.
- Docs: show pattern for `defer iter.Close()` and for canceling with ctx if you want fast shutdown.

Anya R.: Also add tests to ensure no goroutine leaks: use runtime.NumGoroutine() snapshot before/after with short timeout in CI. Catches these.

Mike T.: Good plan. I can file the SDK perf/regression test and update sample app to use `defer iter.Close()`. Who wants to take the transport change?

Kevin L.: I'll own the transport change. I'll add a boolean on the request meta `NoRetryOnStream:true` so existing callers unaffected. Then we can revisit default later.

Nora S.: I'll sketch the iterator Close semantics + error mapping (so Cancel -> context.Canceled). Also add an example in onboarding docs showing `select { case <-ctx.Done(): iter.Close(); return }`.

Anya R.: Great. For immediate onboarding friction, can we add a short note in the Quickstart that streaming cancellation needs explicit Close or context-aware loop pattern? New users keep hitting this.

devx-bot: Created issue #2123: "Go generator stream cancel semantics / goroutine leak" and linked PR placeholder. https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/issues/2123 :robot_face:

Mike T.: Awesome, thanks. I'll update the sample app and run leak test locally. Will ping when PR is ready. 🙏

Kevin L.: thx — when you push, leave a link and I'll add transport tests for the 401 retry race.

Nora S.: One more note: consider exposing backpressure knobs in SDK (max buffer tokens) so sample apps don't hold huge internal buffers on cancelled streams. Not urgent but related to user surprise.

Mike T.: Good call. I'll capture that as a follow-up in the issue.

Anya R.: Thanks all. Small, concrete steps and we should fix the main onboarding friction quickly. :thumbsup:
